extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patent examiners (and practitioners) on determining prior art dates and applying or overcoming rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 (including detailed rules for 102(a),(b),(c),(d),(e)). Covers international application date rules, affidavit options, priority/benefit perfection, and examiner procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised 35 U.S.C. 102(e) two clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised 35 U.S.C. 102(e) has two separate clauses, namely, 35 U.S.C. 102(e)(1) for publications of patent applications and 35 U.S.C. 102(e)(2) for U.S. patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 102(e)(1), in combination with amended 35 U.S.C. 374, provides prior art effect for certain publications of patent applications (including certain international applications) as of their effective United States filing dates. Use the clause appropriate to the reference type (application publication vs. issued patent).

rubrics_metrics.name: When an international filing date counts as a U.S. filing date for 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international filing date is a United States filing date for 35 U.S.C. 102(e) if the international application (1) was filed on or after November 29, 2000, (2) designated the United States, and (3) was published by WIPO under PCT Article 21(2) in the English language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all three conditions are met, the prior art date of a reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) may be the international filing date or an earlier U.S. filing date for which priority or benefit is properly claimed. Publication under PCT Art. 21(2) may result from a request for early publication or after 18 months from the earliest claimed filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on using international applications filed before Nov. 29, 2000 under 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications filed prior to November 29, 2000, or that did not designate the U.S., or were not published in English under PCT Article 21(2) by WIPO, may not be used to reach back (bridge) to an earlier filing date for prior art purposes under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications of international applications filed before November 29, 2000 do not have a 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date at all; they remain available as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of their publication date. Apply pre-AIPA rules for IAs filed before Nov. 29, 2000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply 35 U.S.C. 102(a) when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: For 35 U.S.C. 102(a) to apply, the reference must have a publication date earlier in time than the effective filing date of the application, and must not be applicant’s own work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a reference is prior art under 102(e), examiners should still consider 102(a) because (i) publication of an international application under PCT Article 21(2) may be the earliest prior art date under 102(a) for the disclosure, and (ii) references applied only under 102(e), (f), or (g) and used in a 103(a) rejection may be disqualified under 103(c) if commonly owned at the invention time.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ways to overcome a 35 U.S.C. 102(b) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 102(b) can be overcome by: (A) Persuasively arguing that the claims are patentably distinguishable from the prior art; (B) Amending the claims to patentably distinguish over the prior art; or (C) Perfecting priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 within the applicable time periods by amending the specification or filing an application data sheet and establishing that the prior application satisfies 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the timing rules in 37 CFR 1.78(a) and MPEP §201.11 and §706.02. Priority/benefit perfection requires demonstrating enablement and written description support in the priority application.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ways to overcome a 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 102(e) can be overcome by: (A) Persuasively arguing that the claims are patentably distinguishable; (B) Amending the claims; (C) Filing an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 that the reference invention is not by 'another'; (D) Filing an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 showing prior invention if the reference is not a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication claiming the same patentable invention; (E) Perfecting a claim to priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) within the time period set in 37 CFR 1.55(a)(1); or (F) Perfecting priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 within the time periods in 37 CFR 1.78(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.131 is not acceptable if the claims of the reference U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication and the application are directed to the same invention or are obvious variants. In such cases consider double patenting rejections or interference procedures (MPEP §804 or Chapter 2300). Establish enablement and written description for any perfected priority claim per 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ways to overcome a 35 U.S.C. 102(a) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 102(a) can be overcome by: (A) Persuasively arguing that the claims are patentably distinguishable from the prior art; (B) Amending the claims; (C) Filing an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 showing prior invention if the reference is not a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication claiming the same patentable invention; (D) Filing an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 showing the reference invention is not by 'another'; (E) Perfecting a claim to priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d); and (F) Perfecting priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using 1.131 affidavits, ensure the reference is not a U.S. patent or U.S. application publication claiming the same invention or obvious variants (see MPEP §715).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(c) — abandonment of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 102(c), abandonment of the 'invention' (as distinguished from abandonment of an application) results in loss of right to a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2134 for case law and the specific criteria that define abandonment of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102(d) — four conditions for statutory bar
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(d) establishes four conditions which, if all are present, establish a statutory bar against granting a patent in the U.S.: (A) The foreign application must be filed more than 12 months before the effective filing date of the U.S. application; (B) The foreign and U.S. applications must be filed by the same applicant, legal representatives or assigns; (C) The foreign application must have actually issued as a patent or inventor’s certificate before the filing in the U.S.; and (D) The same invention must be involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a foreign patent or inventor’s certificate meeting all four requirements is discovered, the examiner should make a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(d). See MPEP §2135.01 for case law clarifying each requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search policy for 35 U.S.C. 102(d) prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should only undertake a search for an issued foreign patent for use as 35 U.S.C. 102(d) prior art if there is a reasonable possibility that a foreign patent covering the same subject matter has been granted to the same inventive entity before the U.S. effective filing date (i.e., the foreign filing date is sufficiently earlier than the U.S. filing date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally such searches are unproductive due to short time windows, but average pendency varies by country (e.g., Belgium may grant quickly; Japan may take a decade). Searches may be done on electronic databases by either the examiner or STIC. The document must be a patent or inventor’s certificate, not merely a published application.

rubrics_metrics.name: When 35 U.S.C. 102(e) is used and inventive entity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(e) allows certain prior art (U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications and WIPO publications of international applications) to be applied as of their effective U.S. filing dates. To apply a reference under 102(e), the inventive entity of the application must be different than that of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there are joint inventors, only one inventor need be different for the inventive entities to be different and for a 102(e) rejection to be applicable. 102(e) is mostly utilized when the publication/issue date is too recent for application under 102(a) or (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: 706.02(f)(1) Step (A): Eligible reference types for 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: The potential reference must be a U.S. patent, a U.S. application publication (35 U.S.C. 122(b)), or a WIPO publication of an international application under PCT Article 21(2) in order to apply the reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the potential reference is not one of these types, it cannot be applied under 102(e); consider 102(a) or (b) instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: 706.02(f)(1) Step (B): Reference resulting from or claiming benefit of an international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine if the potential reference resulted from, or claimed the benefit of, an international application. If it did not, its 102(e) date is its earliest effective U.S. filing date, taking into account any proper benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the reference did not result from or claim benefit of an IA, consider any proper earlier U.S. benefit claims that would shift the earliest effective U.S. filing date for 102(e) purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 706.02(f)(1) Step (C)(1): Three conditions for IA to give international filing date as US filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the potential reference resulted from or claimed the benefit of an international application, the international application must meet three conditions for its international filing date to be a U.S. filing date for prior art under 102(e): (a) an international filing date on or after November 29, 2000; (b) designated the United States; and (c) published under PCT Article 21(2) in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these are met, the international filing date (or an earlier effective U.S. filing date if properly claimed) is the 102(e) prior art date. Earlier international applications that are relied upon must themselves satisfy the three conditions for their filing dates to be U.S. filing dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: 706.02(f)(1) Step (C)(2): IA filed on/after Nov 29, 2000 but did not designate US or not published in English
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application was filed on or after November 29, 2000 but did not designate the United States or was not published in English under PCT Article 21(2), do not treat the international filing date as a U.S. filing date for 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this situation, do not apply the reference as of its international filing date or as of completion dates of 371(c) requirements. The reference may be applied under 102(a) or (b) as of its publication date, or under 102(e) as of any later U.S. filing date of an application that properly claimed the benefit of the IA.

rubrics_metrics.name: 706.02(f)(1) Step (C)(3): IA filed prior to Nov 29, 2000 (pre-AIPA treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application has an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000, apply the reference under the pre-AIPA provisions of 35 U.S.C. 102 and 374: (a) For U.S. patents, apply 102(e) as of the earlier of the date of completion of the 371(c)(1),(2) and (4) requirements or the filing date of the later-filed U.S. application that claimed the benefit; (b) For U.S. application publications and WIPO publications directly resulting from such IAs, never apply under 102(e) (apply under 102(a) or (b) as of publication date); (c) For U.S. application publications of applications that claim the benefit under 120 or 365(c) of an IA filed prior to Nov 29, 2000, apply 102(e) as of the actual filing date of the later-filed U.S. application that claimed the benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendments to 102(e) and 374 do not apply to IAs with international filing dates prior to Nov 29, 2000.

rubrics_metrics.name: 706.02(f)(1) Step (C)(4): WIPO publication vs. patent 102 dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Although a WIPO publication or a U.S. patent issued from an international application may not have a 102(e) date (or may have a 102(e) date after the effective filing date being examined), the corresponding WIPO publication may have an earlier 102(a) or 102(b) date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should be aware that different publication/filing/issue events can yield different applicable prior art dates under 102(a),(b),(e). Consider all available dates when assessing prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use or on-sale timing rule for 102(a) vs 102(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the activity (public use or on sale) occurred within the year prior to the effective filing date, 35 U.S.C. 102(a) applies; if the activity occurred more than one year prior, 35 U.S.C. 102(b) is applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If evidence indicates applicant made the invention and only disclosed it to others within the year prior to the effective filing date, do not make a rejection under 102(a). See MPEP §2133.03 and related case law on public use and on-sale bars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner requirement for information on public use/on-sale issues
rubrics_metrics.description: As an aid to resolving public use or on-sale issues, an applicant may be required to answer specific questions posed by the examiner and to explain or supplement any evidence of record. Information sought should be restricted to that reasonably necessary for the examiner to render a decision on patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may make a requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 and should set a 1- or 2-month time period for reply (unless the Office action has a shortened statutory period, in which case that period applies). Failure to reply timely will result in abandonment (35 U.S.C. 133). Use form paragraph 7.104 for the requirement; if sufficient evidence exists to establish a prima facie case of public use or on sale, use form paragraph 7.16 to make a 102(b) rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/declaration limits under 37 CFR 1.131 and 1.132
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 may show prior invention (applicant's earlier invention) if the reference is not a U.S. patent or a U.S. patent application publication claiming the same patentable invention. Affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.132 may show that the reference invention is not by 'another.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the claims of the reference U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication and the application are directed to the same invention or are obvious variants, a 1.131 affidavit is not acceptable to overcome the rejection. Under those circumstances, the examiner must consider whether a double patenting rejection or an interference is appropriate (MPEP §804; Chapter 2300). See MPEP §§715 and 716.10 for further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples illustrating determination of 102(e) prior art dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Nine illustrative examples (Examples 1–9) show common factual situations for determining 35 U.S.C. 102(e) dates for references, covering 111(a) applications with and without priority/benefit claims, 111(a) with foreign priority claims, and various international application scenarios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the examples to determine whether a reference’s 102(e)(1) (publication) or 102(e)(2) (patent) date is an international filing date, an earlier U.S. filing date, a later U.S. filing date, none, or the date of fulfillment of 371(c) requirements depending on the facts (e.g., filing dates, language of WIPO publication, designation of U.S.).
